class.name: PlantSpecies
class.brief_description: One kind of plant: its meshes, spacing and the ground it grows on.
class.description: Describes a plant for [VegetationField3D]: mesh variants, how far apart plants stand, how much room they keep from other species, and rules over the [TerrainDataMap3D] maps (slope, height, curvature, wetness, water depth, distance to water). Each rule is a range with a soft edge: a plant is kept with probability [member density] times the product of every rule's weight at its point. The defaults keep every plant on dry land; a water plant widens [member water_depth_range].

method.name: get_patch_depth
method.description: How far inside one of the species' patches a point lies, in metres: positive inside, negative outside, about 0 where [method get_patch_weight] crosses one half. A large number for species without patches.

method.name: get_patch_weight
method.description: Returns the patch weight at [param global_position], from 0 (between patches) to 1 (inside one). Always 1 when [member patch_scale] is 0.

method.name: get_rule_fade
method.description: Returns the soft edge of a rule, see [method set_rule_fade].

method.name: get_rule_range
method.description: Returns the range of a rule, see [method set_rule_range].

method.name: get_suitability_at
method.description: Returns the product of every rule's weight at [param global_position] on a baked [TerrainDataMap3D], from 0 (cannot grow here) to 1.

method.name: rule_weight
method.description: Returns the weight of [param value] against [param rule]: 1 inside the range, falling to 0 over the fade (smoothstep), 0 beyond.

method.name: season_temperature
method.description: The growing season's mean temperature for a place with these January and July means, on the annual harmonic: the mean over the days whose mean is at least 0.9 C, or [code]-10[/code] when there are fewer than 94 such days (Paulsen and Körner 2014). Trees stop where it falls to 6.4 C, whatever the mean annual temperature, so oceanic mountains with mild winters and cool summers have low treelines. [constant RULE_SEASON_TEMPERATURE] uses it.

method.name: set_rule_fade
method.description: Sets the soft edge of a rule, in the rule's units: the weight falls from 1 to 0 over this distance outside the range. 0 is a hard edge.

method.name: set_rule_range
method.description: Sets the range (min, max) of a rule in its units, see [enum Rule].

method.name: trample_cover
method.description: Returns the cover left after [param passes] walkers a year: [code]1 / (1 + x^1.5)[/code] with [code]x = passes / trample_resistance[/code]. 1 when [member trample_resistance] is 0.

method.name: trample_scale
method.description: Returns the size of the plants left after [param passes] walkers a year, from 1 down to 0.45 on a heavily used path.

members.member: How far the plant tilts from upright towards the ground normal: 0 upright (trees, reeds), 1 along the slope (ground cover).
Soft edge of [member aridity_range].

Aridity index (annual precipitation over potential evapotranspiration, Thornthwaite) where the species grows: below 0.5 is dry steppe, above 1 humid. Ignored when the map has no climate ([method TerrainDataMap3D.bake_climate]).
Soft edge of [member beach_range].
Range of [constant RULE_BEACH].

If [code]true[/code], this species' crown is needle-leaved (pine, spruce, fir, larch). [VegetationField3D] counts each crown's share of the cover overhead, so the floor under it can follow the stand type through [member conifer_range].
Share of the light this species' crown stops under its core, for [member canopy_radius]. A broadleaf crown in summer stops about 0.85 to 0.95, a pine or birch less.

Crown radius in metres (times each plant's scale). Above 0 the species shades the ground under it, and later species in the [Biome] with a [member shade_range] are placed by that shade (see [method VegetationField3D.get_shade_at]).
Soft edge of [member coast_exposure_range].
Range of [constant RULE_COAST_EXPOSURE].
Fade width outside [member conifer_range].

Share of the canopy overhead that is needle-leaved where this species grows, from [code]0.0[/code] (broadleaf: beech, oak) to [code]1.0[/code] (conifer: spruce, pine), from crowns with [member canopy_conifer] placed earlier by the same [VegetationField3D]. Open ground counts as [code]0.0[/code].
Soft edge of [member curvature_range].
Ground curvature range in 1/m: positive in hollows and valley floors, negative on ridges.
With [constant DEADWOOD_BESIDE]: how far from a log's side the species grows, in metres, thinning out across the band.

With [constant DEADWOOD_BESIDE]: the plant comes up out of the wood itself, as wood-decay fungi do (honey fungus). Its foot moves onto the log's side where it meets the ground, a little into the bark, and it turns so its +X faces out of the wood.

With [constant DEADWOOD_ON]: the thinnest log it grows on (radius, metres). Thickness stands for decay: thin branches stay bare, thick rotting trunks carry seedlings. With [constant DEADWOOD_BESIDE]: the thinnest log it grows beside (0: by any fallen wood).

How the species meets fallen wood placed by [VegetationField3D] (this field's or its [member VegetationField3D.canopy_field]'s): species with the meta [code]deadwood[/code] whose meshes carry the meta [code]tree_deadwood_axis[/code] (start, end and radius in mesh space, as [code]TreeGenerator[/code] gives its logs, fallen branches and sticks). An uprooted tree's log also carries [code]tree_root_pit[/code] (centre, radius, depth in mesh space): whatever the rule, no plant grows in that pit, and a [GrassField3D] with this field as its [code]undergrowth_field[/code] leaves it bare.
With [constant DEADWOOD_BESIDE]: only on the uphill side of a log on sloping ground, where creeping leaf litter piles against it.
Fraction of the Poisson-disk points kept where every rule is fully met, from 0 to 1.
Soft edge of [member dune_range].

Range of coastal dune stability the plant grows on ([method TerrainGenerator3D.get_dune_stability]: marram cover, [code]0[/code] bare moving sand to [code]1[/code] fixed), with [code]-1[/code] off the dune sand (less than 0.3 m of it). Only applied where the map's [member TerrainDataMap3D.geology_source] has built dunes; [method PlantGenerator.make_dunes] sets embryo and mobile dunes to the moving sand and fixed dunes to the held sand.

The plant seen from far above (rgb) and how much of the ground it hides (alpha, 0 to 1). Beyond its [member visibility_range] the plants are thinned away, and [VegetationField3D] bakes this colour into the ground's [code]vegetation_far_map[/code] where they grew, so a stand of them stays a patch of their colour to the horizon (see [method VegetationField3D.get_floor_shader_code]). Alpha 0 leaves the ground as it is.

If [code]true[/code], plants sit level on the water surface ([method TerrainDataMap3D.get_water_depth_at] above the ground), as water lilies do. Pair it with a [member water_depth_range] that starts above zero.
If [code]true[/code], each plant is turned so its +X axis points downhill, the way water runs over the ground there, instead of a random yaw: aquatic mosses trail downstream.
Radius in metres that later species in the [Biome] keep clear of (a trunk and its shade). 0 leaves room for anything.
Soft edge of [member height_range].
Ground height range in metres.
Soft edge of [member january_temperature_range].

January mean temperature in °C where the species grows: its frost hardiness, for example [code]Vector2(-3, 100)[/code] for beech, which stops where winters are much colder. Ignored when the map has no climate ([method TerrainDataMap3D.bake_climate]).
Soft edge of [member litter_range].

Range of leaf litter fallen from the crowns the plant may grow on ([method VegetationField3D.get_litter_at]): full under broad-leaved crowns, thinning over a few metres past their rim, so litter drifts into edges and clearings. Needle-leaved crowns drop none.
How far, in degrees, plants at the very edge of a patch lean out towards the open, easing to upright over [member margin_width]. Bracken 20 and bramble 15 in [method PlantGenerator.make_floor].

The size of plants at the very edge of a patch, as a share of their own, growing to full size over [member margin_width]: a bracken stand's advancing front of shorter fronds (0.55 in [method PlantGenerator.make_floor]; bramble 0.7).

How deep into its patches a species' margin reaches, in metres (see [member margin_scale] and [member margin_lean]); 0 for none. Only for species with patches ([member patch_scale]). Bracken 3 m and bramble 2 m in [method PlantGenerator.make_floor].
Mesh variants; each plant picks one at random. Plants carry ([code]variant, scale, random, species[/code]) in [code]INSTANCE_CUSTOM[/code] for their materials.
The channel of [member VegetationField3D.density_mask] that scales this species' density: 0 red, 1 green, 2 blue, 3 alpha; -1 ignores the mask.
If [code]true[/code], the species grows where the mask channel is low instead (one minus it), so a meadow can fill exactly the clearing that keeps trees out.

Heavier meshes drawn within [member near_range], one per entry of [member meshes] in the same order (a shorter list repeats). Each plant keeps its variant, so a tree with real needles near the camera and needle sprays beyond it stays the same tree. The field cuts such a species into cells about a quarter of [member near_range] across (at least 4 m), so the swap happens a few plants at a time, and crossfades the two over the last tenth of the range with a dither.
Passed to [member near_mesh_source]'s [code]request_near_mesh[/code], to say which plant's near meshes are wanted.

Near meshes on demand, for heavy meshes only plants that come near need: an object with [code]request_near_mesh(key: int, variant: int) -> Mesh[/code], returning [code]null[/code] while the mesh is still being built. Used when [member near_meshes] is empty and [member near_range] is above 0: [VegetationField3D] asks for each cell within 1.2 x [member near_range] of the camera every frame until it has the mesh, then draws it with the same crossfade as [member near_meshes], and frees the cell beyond 1.5 x, so the source can free meshes nothing draws. Only the object's id is kept: keep the source alive yourself.
Distance in metres within which [member near_meshes] are drawn instead of [member meshes]. 0 turns the swap off.
Fraction of the ground inside patches.

If [code]true[/code], the species grows between the patches instead. Two species with the same [member patch_scale], [member patch_cover] and [member patch_seed], one inverted, share the ground exactly (for example tall grass in patches and clover between them).

When above 0, the species grows only along the edges of its patches ([member patch_scale], [member patch_cover], [member patch_seed]), in a band about this wide in metres: the arcs and rings in which fairy-ring fungi fruit along their mycelium's advancing front. The weight is [code]exp(-(d / patch_ring)^2)[/code], d the distance to the patch edge. [method PlantGenerator.make_floor] sets it for the clouded agaric.
Size of the patches, in metres. The species then grows only in patches (clover beds, flower drifts, stands of tall grass), from value noise over the ground. 0 turns patches off.
Seed of the patch noise.
Soft edge of [member precipitation_range].
Annual precipitation in mm where the species grows. Ignored when the map has no climate ([method TerrainDataMap3D.bake_climate]).
If [code]true[/code], each plant turns to a random angle around its up axis.
Soft edge of [member rock_range].

How much more the species grows at the foot of a rock ([member VegetationField3D.obstacles]), where shelter and the rain running off the rock keep the ground moist: its suitability is multiplied by [code]1 + rock_foot * exp(-d / 0.5)[/code], d the distance past the rock's edge in metres. Near a rock the species also grows in the gaps between its patches ([member patch_scale]): the patch weight there is at least [code]1 - exp(-rock_foot * exp(-d / 0.5))[/code]. [method PlantGenerator.make_floor]: ferns 2.5, mosses 3, wood sorrel and seedlings 1.5.

Bare rock exposure (0 to 1) where the species grows, from the map's [member TerrainDataMap3D.geology_source]. Trees and most plants need little: for example [code]Vector2(0, 0.3)[/code]. Ignored when the map has no geology.
Each plant's uniform scale is picked between [code]x[/code] and [code]y[/code].
Soft edge of [member shade_range].
Soft edge of [member season_temperature_range], C.
Range of [constant RULE_SEASON_TEMPERATURE], C.

Canopy shade (0 open sky, 1 dense crown) where the species grows, from the canopy species placed before it by a [VegetationField3D]: for example [code]Vector2(0.4, 1)[/code] for bilberry, ferns and mosses, [code]Vector2(0, 0.3)[/code] for meadow plants. Ignored outside a [VegetationField3D] (a [GrassField3D] has no canopy).
Soft edge of [member slope_range], in degrees.
Ground slope range in degrees (0 is flat).
Soft edge of [member soil_depth_range], in metres.

Soil depth over bedrock (metres) where the species grows, from the map's [member TerrainDataMap3D.geology_source]. Trees need room to root, for example [code]Vector2(0.5, 100000)[/code]; grasses take thin soil. Ignored when the map has no geology.
Minimum distance in metres between two plants of this species (Poisson-disk radius).
Soft edge of [member sunlight_range].

Annual mean shortwave radiation at the ground in W/m², with slope, aspect and horizons: sun-loving species on south-facing slopes, shade-tolerant ones on north-facing. Ignored when the map has no climate ([method TerrainDataMap3D.bake_climate]).
Soft edge of [member spray_range].

Waterfall spray potential (0 to 1, [method TerrainDataMap3D.get_spray_at]) where the species grows. By default no plant grows in a fall's soaked zone, where only mosses and wet rock hold; mosses from [method PlantGenerator.make_floor] take [code]Vector2(0, 1)[/code]. Ignored when the map has no geology.

The species' own litter on the ground under its stands, linear colour in rgb and how much of the ground it covers in alpha: bracken's mat of dead fronds and bramble's leaves (set by [method PlantGenerator.make_floor]). A [GrassField3D] with [member GrassField3D.undergrowth_field] lays it on the ground where the stands shade the sward out, so the ground there is litter instead of bare soil ([method VegetationField3D.get_sward_litter_at]).

For a [member stone_top] species: whether it keeps to damp or to dry stone tops. Each top is damp (1) or dry (0), the whole stone alike: damp where [code]1.0 * a + 0.5 * low + 0.7 * shelter + 0.6 * shade[/code] reaches 0.45 (give or take 0.05 per stone), measured at its cap: a how far the cap tilts to the north (-Z), low 1 for a top 5 cm or less over the ground falling to 0 at 0.8 m, shelter how steeply taller stone tops within 2 m rise over it (as a tangent, full at 45 degrees; stones to the south count fully, those to the north half), shade the canopy's shade. Its suitability is multiplied by [code]lerp(1, damp, stone_top_damp)[/code] when positive and [code]lerp(1, 1 - damp, -stone_top_damp)[/code] when negative, so green cushions keep to the low, shaded, north-tilted tops and dry ones to the high, sunlit ones. [method PlantGenerator.make_stones] pairs a green moss (positive) with a smaller, sparser, yellow-olive one (-1).

For a [member stone_top] species: the band of the top's height over the water surface, in metres, that it keeps to (fading over 4 cm past each end); off while [code]x >= y[/code]. The water surface over a top is the ground under it plus the map's water depth there; a top on dry ground counts as its height over the ground plus a quarter of its distance to the water. Aquatic mosses take a band from under the water to just over it (with a [member water_depth_range] that reaches under water, since the bed under the stone is), and dry-ground mosses one from above the flood line.

If [code]true[/code], the species grows only on the tops of stones ([member VegetationField3D.stone_tops]), set on the stone's cap and tilted with its curve: moss cushions on boulders and scree. A plant reaching more than 1.5 cm past its cap grows smaller to fit (down to 45% of its size), or is not placed. Its other rules still apply at the stone's place.

How strictly the species keeps to the gaps between stones ([member VegetationField3D.obstacles]): the fine soil caught between scree, river gravel and shingle, and rock cracks. Its suitability is multiplied by [code]lerp(1, g, stone_gap)[/code], g the product of two terms: the plant roots against a stone (full within 8 cm of the nearest stone's edge, none past 20 cm), and a second stone is close by ([code]exp(-d / 0.12)[/code], reaching 0 at [code]d = 0.48[/code], d the distance in metres to the edge of the second-nearest stone), so a point against a stone with another close by counts as a gap, and open ground and the foot of a lone boulder do not. At [code]1.0[/code] it grows nowhere else, and not at all where there are no obstacles; pressed between stones its leaves may reach 18 cm in over a stone (10 cm more than other plants), and past that it is made smaller rather than left out. [method PlantGenerator.make_stones] uses 1 for its crevice plants.

How much of the grass a stand of this species shades out under it, 0 to 1: bracken and bramble (0.85 and 0.7 in [method PlantGenerator.make_floor]) leave little sward beneath them. A [GrassField3D] reads it through [member GrassField3D.undergrowth_field] and [method VegetationField3D.get_sward_shade_at].
Soft edge of [member talus_range].
Scree cover (0 to 1) where the species grows, from the map's geology. Keep most species to [code]Vector2(0, 0.2)[/code]; a few scree specialists take more. Ignored when the map has no geology.
Soft edge of [member temperature_range].
Mean annual temperature in °C where the species grows; with the lapse rate it sets tree lines and altitude belts. Ignored when the map has no climate ([method TerrainDataMap3D.bake_climate]).
Soft edge of [member tide_height_range], m.
Range of [constant RULE_TIDE_HEIGHT], m above the sea.

Distance, in metres, beyond which the species is not drawn. For ground cover too small to see far away. Plants with the generated plant material thin out before it: from 35% of the range the share drawn falls to none at the range, each plant shrinking away in the order of its placement rank while the rest grow slightly to hold the cover, so there are no pops; [member far_color] then carries them on the ground. 0 draws it at any distance.
Soft edge of [member water_depth_range], in metres.
Water depth range in metres; 0 is dry land. The default (0, 0) with a 5 cm fade keeps plants out of water.
Soft edge of [member water_distance_range], in metres.
Signed distance to the shoreline range in metres: positive on land, negative under water.
Soft edge of [member wetness_range].
Topographic wetness index range: about 4 to 7 on hillsides, 10 and above where water collects.

Square metres one plant at scale 1 shows the wind, for the shelter it gives blowing sand ([method VegetationField3D.sample_lateral_cover]). Negative: 0.4 of its first mesh's height times its mean width (a grass tuft's leaves block about that share of its outline). 0: no shelter.

Walkers a year on a worn path that halve this species' cover. 0: not trampled. Rosettes such as plantain resist most, then grasses; ferns, heaths and tall forbs least. [method PlantGenerator.tag_species] sets it from [method PlantGenerator.get_trample_resistance].

constants.constant: Slope in degrees.
Ground height in metres.
Curvature in 1/m.
Topographic wetness index.
Water depth in metres.
Signed distance to water in metres.
Soil depth over bedrock in metres (needs the map's geology).
Bare rock exposure, 0 to 1 (needs the map's geology).
Scree cover, 0 to 1 (needs the map's geology).
Canopy shade, 0 to 1 (see [member shade_range]).
Mean annual temperature, °C (climate).
January mean temperature, °C (climate).
Annual precipitation, mm (climate).
Aridity index (climate).
Annual mean shortwave at the ground, W/m² (climate).
Share of the canopy overhead that is needle-leaved, [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code].
Waterfall spray potential, [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code] ([method TerrainDataMap3D.get_spray_at]).
Broad-leaf litter fallen from the crowns, [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code] ([method VegetationField3D.get_litter_at]).

Coastal dune stability, [code]0[/code] bare moving sand to [code]1[/code] fixed under marram ([method TerrainGenerator3D.get_dune_stability]); [code]-1[/code] off the dune sand. Only applied where the map's [member TerrainDataMap3D.geology_source] has built dunes.

The growing season's mean temperature, C ([method season_temperature]), from the map's January and July means. Needs the map's climate; only worked out for species whose range is narrower than the default.

Height above the sea, m: the ground of the map's [member TerrainDataMap3D.geology_source] over its sea ([member TerrainGenerator3D.sea_level] plus [member TerrainGenerator3D.height_offset]). Salt marsh zones by it. The coast rules need a geology source with a sea; without one, a species that uses any of them is not placed.

Exposure to the sea's waves, [code]0[/code] sheltered to [code]1[/code] open ([method TerrainGenerator3D.get_coast_exposure_at]); [code]0[/code] far from the sea, so pair it with [constant RULE_TIDE_HEIGHT]. Needs a geology source with a sea.
Beach mask, [code]1[/code] on the beach face fading over the backshore, [code]0[/code] inland ([method TerrainGenerator3D.get_beach_at]). Needs a geology source with a sea.
Number of rules.
Kept off a log's footprint (closer to its axis than its radius, seen from above).

Only on logs at least [member deadwood_min_radius] thick, set on the upper surface (height and tilt from the cylinder, the upper two thirds of its width; use [member align_to_ground] 1 to follow the curve). Mosses, wood sorrel, seedlings on nurse logs.
Only within [member deadwood_band] of a log's side. Ferns along a trunk, leaves banked against it.
Fallen wood does not matter to it.
